traces for emailservice: SIGNIFICANT change; own spans self-time p50 0.19->0.22ms (1.15x), errors 0.0->0.0; inbound calls self-time p50 3.59->3.9ms (1.09x), errors 0.0->0.0545

alternatives_rejected.why: An injected delay would shift the whole latency distribution, but p50 self-time barely moves (0.19->0.22ms, inbound 3.59->3.9ms in E2). Only the tail explodes (latency-90 z=615.9 in E1), and new errors appear (0.0->0.0545 in E2), which is typical of packet loss, not pure delay.

The socket metric rise (z=21.28 in E1/E4) is far smaller than the latency-90 deviation (z=615.9). It is consistent with retransmissions and lingering connections caused by loss, rather than being the primary fault signal.

Its latency-90 deviation (z=20.12 in E1) is an order of magnitude smaller than emailservice's. E2 shows the errors appear on calls inbound to emailservice, so checkoutservice is the caller absorbing the downstream tail latency.

proposed_fix.description: Inspect emailservice pod networking for packet loss, such as an injected netem/tc qdisc, a faulty node NIC, or CNI drops. Remove the offending loss rule, or cordon the bad node so the pod reschedules elsewhere. Then confirm that emailservice p90 latency and checkout->emailservice error rate return to baseline.
